jobs.description:
Please Note: This position will be posted through 5/26/2026*

Goodwill of Colorado is seeking versatile and adaptable candidates with experience to become our Shift Supervisors. Previous supervisory experience in retail, restaurant, hospitality, production, manufacturing or similar industries is preferred for this position. A successful Shift Supervisor will naturally become a top candidate for career growth opportunities within Goodwill's Retail Division.

All applicants are required to attach a resume to their application in order to be considered for this position.

Please Note: Our Stores are open 9 am to 9 pm Monday through Saturday and 9 am to 8 pm Sunday. This supervisory position is full-time and will require open availability (including evenings and weekends). Shifts for this position could start as early as 7 am and go as late as 10 pm.

Pay - $20.32 per hour.
This position is eligible for Daily Pay! Work today, get paid today! We’ve partnered with DailyPay, a voluntary benefit to offer employees access to their pay on their own schedule. Full Time employees in our Retail, Sales/Operations, Commercial Contracts are eligible for Medical, Dental, Vision, Retirement, Long Term Disability, Short Term Disability, Life and Accidental Death and Dismemberment, Flexible Spending Accounts and several voluntary supplemental benefit offerings. In addition, these positions are eligible for paid time off in the form of vacation, sick, holiday, floating holiday, jury duty and bereavement leave. Goodwill of Colorado is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program (PSLF) eligible employer.

Job Summary

The Retail Center Shift Supervisor will be responsible for day-to-day, tactical, and practical leadership of associates and teams across the entire retail center.

Essential Functions

Generally responsible for monitoring the whole retail center and addressing immediate issues of safety, customer focus, product flow, and aesthetics either personally or through delegation.

Employee Leadership

Manages breaks.
Redirects staff/work teams to address call-offs.
Coaches’ employees verbally and with initial write-ups.
Provides input to reviews and terminations.
Facilitate employee purchases.

Responsible for counting drawers.
Responsible for making change between drawers and the safe.
Assist with inventory process by counting, entering, and verifying.

Customer Focus

Plan, coordinate, and control the activities of the customer service team to maintain and enhance customer relationships, meet organizational, and operational objectives.
First escalation point for customer complaints.
Point of contact for turning down donations at Attended Donation Centers (ADC).

Cross Training

Maintains knowledge of store procedures at the proficiency of a generalist with the ability to fill in for an emergency.
Ensure E-Commerce product is processed accurately and moving to E-Commerce efficiently.
Uses and becomes certified on pallet jack, walkie stacker, forklift, hand dolly, or other equipment or tools to effectively move and store donated product.
Maintains knowledge to the level where operations can be maintained in rare cases where no Assistant Manager or Manager are able to be on premises.
Job duties may extend beyond the tasks listed and may include additional responsibilities as required.

Qualifications

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

Education

A High School diploma or equivalent is preferred.

Experience

Previous supervisory experience is preferred.
Two (2) years’ retail experience is desired.

Other

Familiar with product pricing, trends, fashions, and seasonal changes.
Ability to communicate effectively both verbally and electronically with customers, managers, supervisors, staff, and peers.
Able to obtain certification in all employee positions through completion of On the Job (OJT) documentation.
Able to obtain walkie stacker and/or forklift certification to safely operate equipment.
Able to quickly problem solve and make decisions.
Able to maintain confidentiality and follow Goodwill’s policies and procedures.
Proficient in the utilization of office equipment, office software (i.e. Word, Excel) and web-based applications (i.e. UKG) to meet the needs of employees and the organization.
Ability to manage corporate email and calendar (i.e. Outlook).
Able to withstand prolonged standing, bending, and lifting up to 8 hours per day.
Able to work a varied schedule to include weekends, evenings, and holidays with occasional overtime as necessary.

jobs.description:
We are seeking a dynamic, organized home care Case Manager to join our team. The ideal candidate is a dependable professional with excellent communication, customer service, and organizational skills who can effectively coordinate between patients, caregivers, office staff, and management.

In this role, you will help oversee case loads, support direct-care staff, maintain accurate patient and employee documentation, coordinate schedules, and ensure smooth day-to-day office operations. The successful candidate will be comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, managing multiple priorities, and communicating professionally in English language.

Responsibilities

Assist direct-care staff with administrative needs, including providing forms, answering questions, coordinating schedules, and resolving routine concerns.
Monitor and oversee assigned patient and caregiver case loads to support efficient and consistent service delivery.
Assist with creating, organizing, and maintaining patient and staff charts, ensuring documentation is accurate and up to date.
Coordinate communication between patients, caregivers, office staff, and management.
Manage a multi-line phone system and direct calls accurately and professionally.
Provide excellent customer service by responding promptly to inquiries by phone, email, and in person.
Perform accurate data entry using Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, and electronic visit verification (EVV) systems.
Learn and utilize the Sandata Electronic Visit Verification (EVV) system; training will be provided.
Learn and utilize the KanTime system; training will be provided.
Maintain organized digital and physical filing systems.
Assist with staff and executive calendar management, appointments, and scheduling.
Prepare correspondence, proofread documents, and assist with general clerical and administrative duties.
Manage incoming and outgoing mail and other office communications.
Assist with tracking documentation, schedules, and required paperwork for patients and direct-care staff.
Help maintain compliance with company policies and home health documentation requirements.
Communicate professionally and respectfully with patients, families, caregivers, coworkers, and management.

Qualifications & Skills

Fluent in English with strong verbal and written communication skills.
Previous experience in case management, home health, home care, healthcare administration, medical office administration, or a related field preferred.
Strong customer service and interpersonal skills.
Excellent organizational and time-management abilities.
Ability to multitask and work efficiently in a fast-paced environment.
Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite, including Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.
Proficiency with Google Workspace, including Gmail, Calendar, and Drive.
Strong computer and data-entry skills.
Excellent attention to detail and accuracy.
Professional telephone etiquette and experience with multi-line phone systems.
Ability to maintain confidentiality when handling patient and employee information.
Strong problem-solving and communication skills.
Experience with home health or home care services is a plus.
Experience with Sandata or another EVV system is preferred but not required; training will be provided.
Medical or dental receptionist, personal assistant, administrative, or clerical experience is advantageous.
Bilingual preferred.

Join Our Team

Join our energetic and supportive team dedicated to providing high-quality support to patients, families, and caregivers. We value dependable, proactive, and compassionate professionals who are committed to excellent customer service and effective case coordination.

If you are highly organized, comfortable working in a fast-paced environment, and interested in building a career in home health care, we would love to hear from you!

Summary:

The People Concern’s Santa Monica Homeless Multidisciplinary Street Team (HMST) is seeking a master’s level clinical case manager on this multidisciplinary street outreach team. This team is part of a City of Santa Monica strategy to combat homelessness. The goal of HMST is to target the highest utilizers of the City of Santa Monica’s emergency resources (police, fire, and hospitals). The skilled interdisciplinary team uses best practices for engaging chronically homeless individuals with co-occurring mental health, substance use, and/or medical issues. A low client-to-staff ratios is used to maximize effectiveness. The team works closely with each client to develop individualized service plans. The team helps enroll clients in public benefits (i.e. General Relief, SSI/SSDI, Medi-Cal), submit housing applications, and access appropriate medical and behavioral health treatment.

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

Provide field-based services, meeting currently homeless clients where they are in order to eliminate barriers to services.
Assess mental health service needs of clients.
Engage clients in developing mutually agreed-upon goals documented in each client’s confidential service plan.
Provide risk assessment and clinical evaluations for client’s who are potentially gravely disabled and in need of hospitalization and referral to higher levels of care.
Link clients with appropriate medical, mental health, substance abuse, and vocational resources.
Assist clients in obtaining all benefits to which they are entitled, including applying for and advocating for SSI benefits.
Provide opportunities for clients to build a supportive peer community.
Build relationships with County mental health and other resources to increase collaboration and responsiveness to clients with severe mental illness and addiction.
Complete all charting in a timely manner.
Collaborate and communicate effectively with police officers and local hospital staff to reduce police contact and ED visits by targeted population.
Work effectively on an interdisciplinary team and collaborate with Program Manager to ensure high level of clinical oversight.
Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications:

Master’s degree in a mental health field (MSW, MFT, PhD, PsyD)
Valid CA Driver’s license, reliable car, auto insurance, and an acceptable driving record
Demonstrated knowledge of clinical case management.
Experience in dealing with issues faced by population served (serious mental illness, substance abuse, and physical health problems).
Excellent writing and charting skills.
Knowledge of community resources.
Able to maintain an effective working relationship with Santa Monica community partners (including police, firefighters, city staff, etc) and maintain and build professional rapport
Ability to self-motivate, work independently, and communicate effectively.
Able to work collaboratively as part of an interdisciplinary team

Preferred Qualifications:

BBS licensure

Work Environment:

Combination of field and office environment. Field consists of street, Client's homes and facilities such as hospitals, clinics, DMV, DPSS, etc.
Regularly required to sit, stand, bend; occasionally lift or carry up to 35 lbs.
On occasion walk or drive to different local sites
Will necessitate working in busy and loud environments
Will be exposed to elements like cold, heat, dust, noise and odor
May need to bend, stoop, twist, and sit throughout the day

EXPECTED BEHAVIORS OF ALL STAFF

Demonstrate a sense of responsibility

Acknowledge your own areas of improvement
Hear and provide honest, specific and direct feedback
Create an environment where everyone is welcomed valued and respected

About The People Concern

The People Concern empowers the most vulnerable among us to rebuild their lives. One of Los Angeles County’s largest social services agencies, The People Concern was formed in 2016 in a merger of two trusted social service organizations based in Los Angeles County, OPCC and Lamp Community. Informed by more than fifty-eight years of work in the community, The People Concern is a leading provider of, and advocate for, evidence-based solutions to the multi-faceted challenges inherent in homelessness and domestic violence.

With compassion and profound respect for those we serve, we provide a fully integrated system of care – including outreach, interim housing, mental and medical health care, substance abuse services, domestic violence services, life skills & wellness programs, and permanent supportive housing – tailored to the unique needs of homeless individuals, survivors of domestic violence, challenged youth, and others who have nowhere else to turn.

The People Concern’s model of integrated and comprehensive care empowers our participants to navigate the multi-faceted obstacles in their lives, become their best selves, and ultimately, connect with and contribute to their communities.

Position Description:  

Silver Lining Mentoring (SLM) is seeking a collaborative, systems-oriented Program Manager to lead our e-Mentoring program. This person will manage the day-to-day operations and program quality of SLM's e-Mentoring program, and will play a key role in identifying challenges and problem-solving as the program grows and scales by building out the policies, procedures, and tools needed to support that growth.
This position reports to the Senior Director of Programs and works within the Programs Department alongside SLM's other Program Managers, the Volunteer Manager, and the Enrollment Specialist especially for mentee and mentor recruitment efforts. Success in this role requires flexibility and strong collaboration skills, as the Program Manager will partner closely with this team and other departments to balance program needs with organizational goals.

This role is designed for growth. It will start by managing a caseload of e-matches directly, but this is not a permanent caseload-management position: as the program expands over the next 6–12 months, direct reports will be added and this role will transition into supervising the staff who provide match support. Because of that trajectory, prior people management, sound judgment around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability is essential from day one. 

The ideal candidate will bring attention to detail and competency in program development to ensure a smooth and efficient youth and volunteer experience that upholds Silver Lining Mentoring policies, procedures, values, and approach, along with a genuine interest in building and improving systems — not just running an existing playbook. Experience related to youth development, the foster care system, and/or young adult mentoring is valued, and experience maintaining a digital communications or virtual engagement platform is highly desirable.

Program Management, Infrastructure & Quality (40%)

Platform Management
: Manage the e-mentoring platform(s), including day-to-day support needs and community or communication features, in collaboration with the platform provider.

: Partner with Enrollment Team members to screen and train prospective e-mentors, and lead ongoing engagement of approved-but-unmatched mentors to keep them informed and ready to match.

Recommend and implement process improvements to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the e-mentoring program as it evolves.
Policies & Procedures
: Build out and maintain policy and procedure manuals for the e-mentoring program, ensuring program delivery is consistent with SLM’s best practices, values, and the Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring.
Systems & Tools

: Monitor program progress against key performance indicators (KPIs) and assist the Senior Director of Programs in preparing status updates for organizational leadership. Additionally, maintain accurate program and match data in Salesforce, applying SLM's data safety and confidentiality standards, and support the evaluation of that data to inform program improvements.
Evaluation Administration
: Administer the program's evaluation instruments, including survey distribution, response tracking, follow-up with non-respondents, and timely data entry, to ensure complete and usable evaluation data.

Caseload & Match Management (35%)

Match Support
: Manage a caseload of e-matches, providing regular, personalized support to mentors and mentees to help each relationship thrive virtually. This includes conducting regular check-ins with matches to monitor relationship health, celebrate milestones, and identify and address concerns early and guiding matches through intentional match closure/graduation. 
Harm Reduction & Adult-Centered Support
: Provide match support grounded in harm reduction and trauma-informed practice, centering autonomy, informed decision-making, and self-determination given that most e-mentees are legal adults.
Risk Management
: Identify potential risks or liabilities specific to the virtual nature of matches and respond according to SLM policy, escalating to the Senior Director of Programs as needed.
Mentee Engagement Innovation
: Design and implement creative strategies to sustain mentee engagement, including quarterly workshops, compelling rollouts of new resources and opportunities, and persistent, creative follow-up with unresponsive or low-engagement mentees.

: Partner with the Senior Director of Programs to to establish a pathway toward supervising future match support roles in e-mentoring (e.g., track workload and help determine sustainable caseload sizes as the program grows, provide insights for hiring/onboarding new e-mentoring staff, etc.) 

Collaboration & Program Support (25%)

Partnership Support
: Support the identification and maintenance of relationships with strategic partners relevant to the e-mentoring program, in coordination with the Senior Director of Programs and Chief Strategy Officer.
Team Collaboration
: Participate as an active member of the Programs Department, sharing updates and collaborating with other Program Managers on shared practices, tools, and challenges; coordinate with the Volunteer Manager and Enrollment Specialist on mentor recruitment/allocation and mentee recruitment and enrollment specific to e-mentoring.
Cross-Departmental Collaboration
: Participate in relevant working groups to promote cross-departmental collaboration and strategy insight on programming that impacts mentees, mentors, and program staff, including partnering with the Development team to identify and uplift match experiences and stories.

: Compile program reports for partners and donors, pulling and interpreting Salesforce data to present the right metrics, and proactively flagging reportable milestones and trends to the Senior Director of Programs and Development team.

: Actively engage in SLM's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) efforts, such as attending all-staff trainings, providing and receiving feedback, and embracing accountability.
Professionalism & Confidentiality
: Maintain the professional competence and confidentiality necessary to perform job responsibilities.

This role is expected to grow into a supervisory position over the next 6–12 months, so the ability to make and stand behind good calls independently, and to know when and how to escalate is essential

Position Description:  

Silver Lining Mentoring (SLM) is seeking a collaborative, systems-oriented Program Manager to lead our e-Mentoring program. This person will manage the day-to-day operations and program quality of SLM's e-Mentoring program, and will play a key role in identifying challenges and problem-solving as the program grows and scales by building out the policies, procedures, and tools needed to support that growth.
This position reports to the Senior Director of Programs and works within the Programs Department alongside SLM's other Program Managers, the Volunteer Manager, and the Enrollment Specialist especially for mentee and mentor recruitment efforts. Success in this role requires flexibility and strong collaboration skills, as the Program Manager will partner closely with this team and other departments to balance program needs with organizational goals.

This role is designed for growth. It will start by managing a caseload of e-matches directly, but this is not a permanent caseload-management position: as the program expands over the next 6–12 months, direct reports will be added and this role will transition into supervising the staff who provide match support. Because of that trajectory, prior people management, sound judgment around participant safety, harm reduction, and organizational liability is essential from day one. 

The ideal candidate will bring attention to detail and competency in program development to ensure a smooth and efficient youth and volunteer experience that upholds Silver Lining Mentoring policies, procedures, values, and approach, along with a genuine interest in building and improving systems — not just running an existing playbook. Experience related to youth development, the foster care system, and/or young adult mentoring is valued, and experience maintaining a digital communications or virtual engagement platform is highly desirable.

Responsibilities:

Program Management, Infrastructure & Quality (40%)

Platform Management
: Manage the e-mentoring platform(s), including day-to-day support needs and community or communication features, in collaboration with the platform provider.
Volunteer Screening, Training & Engagement
: Partner with Enrollment Team members to screen and train prospective e-mentors, and lead ongoing engagement of approved-but-unmatched mentors to keep them informed and ready to match.
Adaptive Problem-Solving & Continuous Improvement
: Serve as the primary problem-solver for new or unanticipated challenges that arise as a new program, proposing and implementing practical solutions and escalating larger issues as needed. Recommend and implement process improvements to enhance the efficiency and effectiveness of the e-mentoring program as it evolves.
Policies & Procedures
: Build out and maintain policy and procedure manuals for the e-mentoring program, ensuring program delivery is consistent with SLM’s best practices, values, and the Elements of Effective Practice for Mentoring.
Systems & Tools
: Develop and refine Salesforce, Jotform, DocuSign, and other tools/workflows to support e-match tracking, enrollment paperwork, reporting, and data management
Progress Tracking & Data Management
: Monitor program progress against key performance indicators (KPIs) and assist the Senior Director of Programs in preparing status updates for organizational leadership. Additionally, maintain accurate program and match data in Salesforce, applying SLM's data safety and confidentiality standards, and support the evaluation of that data to inform program improvements.
Evaluation Administration
: Administer the program's evaluation instruments, including survey distribution, response tracking, follow-up with non-respondents, and timely data entry, to ensure complete and usable evaluation data.

Caseload & Match Management (35%)

Match Support
: Manage a caseload of e-matches, providing regular, personalized support to mentors and mentees to help each relationship thrive virtually. This includes conducting regular check-ins with matches to monitor relationship health, celebrate milestones, and identify and address concerns early and guiding matches through intentional match closure/graduation. 
Harm Reduction & Adult-Centered Support
: Provide match support grounded in harm reduction and trauma-informed practice, centering autonomy, informed decision-making, and self-determination given that most e-mentees are legal adults.
Risk Management
: Identify potential risks or liabilities specific to the virtual nature of matches and respond according to SLM policy, escalating to the Senior Director of Programs as needed.
Mentee Engagement Innovation
: Design and implement creative strategies to sustain mentee engagement, including quarterly workshops, compelling rollouts of new resources and opportunities, and persistent, creative follow-up with unresponsive or low-engagement mentees.
Caseload Calibration
: Partner with the Senior Director of Programs to to establish a pathway toward supervising future match support roles in e-mentoring (e.g., track workload and help determine sustainable caseload sizes as the program grows, provide insights for hiring/onboarding new e-mentoring staff, etc.) 

Collaboration & Program Support (25%)

Partnership Support
: Support the identification and maintenance of relationships with strategic partners relevant to the e-mentoring program, in coordination with the Senior Director of Programs and Chief Strategy Officer.
Team Collaboration
: Participate as an active member of the Programs Department, sharing updates and collaborating with other Program Managers on shared practices, tools, and challenges; coordinate with the Volunteer Manager and Enrollment Specialist on mentor recruitment/allocation and mentee recruitment and enrollment specific to e-mentoring.
Cross-Departmental Collaboration
: Participate in relevant working groups to promote cross-departmental collaboration and strategy insight on programming that impacts mentees, mentors, and program staff, including partnering with the Development team to identify and uplift match experiences and stories.
Partner & Donor Reporting
: Compile program reports for partners and donors, pulling and interpreting Salesforce data to present the right metrics, and proactively flagging reportable milestones and trends to the Senior Director of Programs and Development team.
DEI Engagement
: Actively engage in SLM's Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI) efforts, such as attending all-staff trainings, providing and receiving feedback, and embracing accountability.
Professionalism & Confidentiality

Responsibilities

The Foster Care Case Manager works under the supervision of the Program Manager. They are responsible for the delivery of case management services, individual and family counseling and training and supervision of foster families. The Foster Care Case Manager assists the Program Manager in developing individual treatment plans for troubled children and their families. They maintain weekly contact with the foster families, children, and bio-families and monitors the progress of the child and family throughout the placement. They assist with training, home studies, and evaluation of foster parents. The Foster Care Case Manager uses standardized tools to measure social and emotional progress and outcomes and prepares written treatment plans and progress reports.

PERSONAL WORK RELATIONSHIP: The Foster Care Case Manager makes decisions regarding the placement and treatment of neglected, abused, disturbed, and medically complex children. He or she will have good verbal and writing skills. They will be capable of working with children, parents, foster parents, client agencies and the courts. The Foster Care Case Manager will be creative, pragmatic, assertive, and know when to act independently and when to seek the advice of others.

EXAMPLES OF DUTIES. The position includes, but is not limited to, the following:

Reviews referrals and matches children with appropriate foster families.
Places children in state licensed or state certified foster homes.
Obtains all state and agency required documentation for child in care.
Provides weekly documented contact and at bi-weekly visits to child and foster home.
Visits each assigned child at least once each month away from the foster home.
Prepares a treatment plan for the child within 21 days of placement and quarterly thereafter.
Prepares monthly progress reports for assigned children.
Provides Independent Living training and monthly ILP progress reports for assigned clients.
Provides reunification services to the biological families when required by treatment plan.
Coordinates visitation of children with biological parents, siblings, and relatives.
Provides supervised visits with parents, siblings, and relative when required by court.
Acts as liaison person with placing agencies, schools, and other community agencies.
Attends court hearings and review hearings.
Attends staff meetings and treatment planning meetings as required.
Completes interviews, training and home studies on prospective foster parents as needed.
Attends conferences and seminars as required for annual training requirement.
Conducts/participates in two or more foster parent support group meetings each year.
Maintains flexible working hours and works weekends or holidays as needed.

Qualifications

The Foster Care Case Manager has a bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and two years’ experience working with children and families. A bachelor’s degree in social work, sociology, psychology, counseling, or related human services field and five years’ experience with a placing agency working with troubled children and families may be consider in lieu of a graduate degree.

About Our Line Of Business

StepStone Family and Youth Services, an affiliate of BrightSpring Health Services, provides the full spectrum of support to children in need of alternative, safer, and more positive living environments with residential and family services. StepStone connects children and youth who need homes with foster families, as well as foster care training, respite care and support services. For young adults transitioning from foster care to independent living, StepStone provides personalized guidance and training on basic life skills, including money management and education. For more information, please visit www.stepstoneyouth.com . Follow us on Facebook and LinkedIn .
